name: Orca
use_label: Run coding agents side by side
one_liner: Runs a fleet of coding agents in parallel from one place.

text.why: Once several coding agents run at the same time, terminal windows and working folders start to tangle. Orca gathers them into one agent development environment, where parallel agents can be attached and detached from a single place. Agents run on the subscription you already pay for, and it is available on desktop, mobile and a remote runtime. Published under MIT.
text.take: A workbench worth trying once you run more than one coding agent at a time and the terminal stops scaling.
build: An internal dev environment with several agents attached at once
A mobile window onto work in progress while away from the desk
A shared team agent slot on a remote runtime

who.situation: runs several agents in separate worktrees
reviews agent work next to PRs and issues
checks progress and replies from a phone

start.text: Download the macOS, Windows or Linux build from onOrca.dev
Mobile: iOS App Store, TestFlight or the Android APK, then pair with the desktop

caveat: Bring your own agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) and their subscriptions
Anonymous usage telemetry is collected; the docs explain how to opt out
Ships daily, so features and screens change often

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.
